cf.title: Add read-only disconnect_requested GUC for graceful client disconnect (reviously goaway)

input.subject: Add GoAway protocol message for graceful but fast server shutdown/switchover

verdict_reasoning: The goal has support in the thread, but two design points of the GUC version are open. standards-compat-1: the author named an opt-in as necessary in message #19 and weighed dropping it in message #21, so old poolers may forward the signal. replication-ondisk-2: message #21 does not say how a ParameterStatus reaches an idle connection, which is the main target. Confidence is low because the GUC design is in a thread this review cannot see.

brief.title: Signal clients to reconnect, now planned as disconnect_requested GUC (was GoAway)
brief.problem: Draining connections from a server in smart shutdown can take as long as the pool's maximum connection lifetime, often 1 hour, even when every transaction is short. This slows read replica switchovers and pooler restarts. Connection poolers, proxies and drivers that keep pools are the main audience.
brief.proposed_design: The server tells each client that it should disconnect when convenient, and the connection keeps working. Postgres sends this signal to all regular backends' clients when smart shutdown starts, and v8 also adds a function to signal a single backend. The design moved from a new protocol message under protocol 3.3, to a protocol extension, and per the CommitFest title now to a read-only GUC.
user_visible_surface: GoAway backend message (byte 'g', no payload), at first under protocol 3.3, later behind an opt-in protocol extension (goaway or _pq_ name).
libpq function PQgoAwayReceived(const PGconn *conn), returning 1 after a GoAway message arrives.
SQL function pg_goaway_backend() to send the request to one backend (added in v8).
psql logs an info line when the server sent GoAway.
Read-only disconnect_requested GUC, named only in the CommitFest title; probably reported through ParameterStatus.
author_claims: Clients that react to the signal let smart shutdown drain in much less time than the pool's maximum lifetime.
Smart shutdown followed by fast shutdown after about 1 second lets most clients disconnect outside a query, so fewer errors and only added latency.
No payload is needed, because clients have nothing to do between closing now and closing when idle.
A NOTICE does not work, because client_min_messages can suppress it.
An opt-in at connection level stops old poolers from forwarding the signal and dropping clients without need.
brief.thread_state: Kirill Reshke, Zsolt Parragi, Tomas Vondra, Jacob Champion, Jim Nasby and Tatsuo Ishii replied; the last message is from 2026-03-31, and the author was weighing ParameterStatus. The GUC version lives in a separate attached thread (DJVLCL7PV7U6...) that is not visible, and Andrey Borodin set Needs review in September.
unclear: The GUC design is not visible: name semantics, when the server reports it, and how it is reported outside the end of a query.
The material does not say whether the GUC version keeps the opt-in, so old PgBouncer or Pgpool-II may still forward the signal to clients.
The material does not say whether pg_goaway_backend() survives, or what privileges it needs.
No pooler or client proof of concept is shown, which Tomas Vondra asked for.
The material does not answer the deadline or priority payload request from Tomas Vondra and Zsolt Parragi.
Only v1 patch prose is shown; later commit messages and docs are missing.

prior_attempts.title: Add and report the new "session_read_only" GUC pseudo-variable.
prior_attempts.quote: Looking through the thread, it seems like there's a pretty fundamental design issue that hasn't been resolved, namely whether and how this ought to interact with default_transaction_read_only.
prior_attempts.reason: Tom Lane found an unresolved design issue: session_read_only combines default_transaction_read_only and RecoveryInProgress(), and the patch does not track intra-session changes to DefaultXactReadOnly. He asked for two separate GUC_REPORT variables, a new name and SIGHUP in place of the new signaling mechanism. The author agreed but sent no new version, and the entry was returned with feedback after that.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: Both add a server-reported read-only GUC sent by ParameterStatus and set by a cross-backend signal. P11 stalled on how its GUC combined with default_transaction_read_only, which has no counterpart in a disconnect_requested flag.

prior_attempts.title: Add new protocol message to make GUC_REPORT configurable and use it for psql prompt substitution of %N with the current user
prior_attempts.quote: I think this is probably one of the core reasons why I would very much prefer GUCs over new message types to configure protocol extensions like this: It means proxies would not to keep track of and re-sync a new kind of connection state every time a protocol extension is added.
prior_attempts.reason: The author withdrew the patch and said he would resend it once Jelte Fennema-Nio's _pq_.report_parameters patch is committed. Peter Eisentraut suggested a GUC that lists the settings to report instead of a new protocol message. Jelte Fennema-Nio argued that proxies such as PgBouncer already re-sync GUCs, so a GUC-based design is less fragile for them than a new message type with its own connection state.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P3 added a new protocol message for GUC_REPORT control. Its key argument prefers GUCs over new message types for proxies, which is the direction this proposal later took.

prior_attempts.title: Client Connection redirection support for PostgreSQL
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P14 told clients where to reconnect. This proposal only asks them to disconnect when convenient, without a target. No reason is recorded for P14.

objections.title: Reported GUC drops the opt-in that kept old poolers from forwarding
objections.failure_scenario: A site runs an existing PgBouncer or Pgpool-II in front of a server with this change, and its application driver learns to act on disconnect_requested. The pooler forwards the ParameterStatus, so the application closes its pooler connection while the pooler keeps the server connection. The replica drain does not speed up, and the extra client reconnects show up during the switchover.
objections.argument: In message #19 the author says a connection-level opt-in is needed so an old PgBouncer does not forward the signal by accident. In message #21 the author accepts losing that opt-in as "maybe not too bad" in exchange for using ParameterStatus. Once drivers react to a reported parameter, the project cannot add an opt-in later without breaking them. The material does not say whether the GUC version keeps any opt-in, for example through report_parameters or a protocol extension.
objections.author_must_show: Does the disconnect_requested version report the parameter only to clients that ask for it, and if not, what do clients behind current poolers see?

critic.reasoning: The author raised this forwarding problem in message #19 and left it open in message #21. The visible material does not say whether the GUC version reports only to clients that ask.

objections.title: ParameterStatus sent while idle changes when this message can arrive
objections.failure_scenario: A pool keeps idle connections that see no query during the drain. If the server reports disconnect_requested only at the end of a query, those connections never learn of the request and the drain waits for the pool's maximum lifetime. If the server sends it while the backend is idle, it uses a timing that clients and proxies may not expect.
objections.argument: In message #21 the author noted that ParameterStatus is normally sent at the end of a query and said this "can be worked around somehow", without saying how. Sending it from an idle backend means a new send path in the idle loop, plus rules for messages that arrive between ReadyForQuery and the next command. Those rules matter to every client and proxy, not only to users of this feature. The material does not show either choice or its effect on idle pooled connections.
objections.author_must_show: When does the server send the disconnect_requested ParameterStatus to an idle backend's client, and which existing clients or proxies were checked against that timing?

critic.reasoning: Message #21 names the end-of-query timing problem and gives no solution, and idle pooled connections are the main target. The "unexpected timing" half is weaker, because the protocol documentation already tells frontends to accept ParameterStatus at any time.

objections.title: No pooler or driver shown that would act on the signal
objections.failure_scenario: An operator starts a smart shutdown on a read replica to switch over. PgBouncer, JDBC pools and other drivers do not yet watch disconnect_requested, so they keep connections until the 1-hour lifetime. The drain takes as long as today, while Postgres still carries a new reported GUC and a libpq function.
objections.argument: The feature helps only when clients react to it, and the material shows no client that does. Kirill Reshke (message #2) wanted this for Odyssey in 2020. Message #4 points to one related patch, and message #14 suggests another trigger. Tomas Vondra asked for a pooler or client proof of concept (message #12), and the author offered to write one (message #15), but none appears in the visible thread. Pgpool-II's maintainer called it no problem for Pgpool-II (message #20), which is not a plan to use it.
objections.author_must_show: Which pooler or driver maintainers have committed to handling disconnect_requested, and can a working proof of concept show switchover drain time before and after?

critic.reasoning: Tomas Vondra asked for a pooler or client proof of concept in message #12, and the visible thread shows none after the offer in message #15. Messages #2, #4 and #14 show interest, so this is a request for evidence and no reason to reject.

refuted.title: The user-facing contract under review is not in the visible material
refuted.failure_scenario: A driver or pooler author builds support from the visible thread, using byte 'g', PQgoAwayReceived() or pg_goaway_backend(). The committed form turns out to be a read-only GUC, so that code never fires and the author finds out only in production. libpq may also keep an exported symbol named after a message that no longer exists.
refuted.argument: The design has moved from a protocol 3.3 message, to a protocol extension, to a GUC named only in the CommitFest title. The GUC design lives in a thread that is not visible here. Several parts of the contract are not stated: the parameter's values, when the server reports it, whether PQgoAwayReceived() and pg_goaway_backend() stay, and what privileges the function needs. Without these, a committer cannot judge whether the contract fits the existing ParameterStatus and pg_*_backend conventions.
refuted.author_must_show: What exactly do clients see in the GUC version: the parameter name and values, when it is reported, and which libpq and SQL functions remain?

critic.reasoning: A driver author who builds against an uncommitted patch version is not a failure of the proposal. The GUC design is in an attached thread that this review cannot see, so this is a limit of the input.

refuted.title: Without an opt-in, old poolers forward the disconnect request to their clients
refuted.failure_scenario: An operator puts a read replica in smart shutdown behind an older PgBouncer or Pgpool-II. The pooler passes the disconnect_requested ParameterStatus on to its clients, and the clients drop their pooler connections. The pooler's own server connections stay open, so the drain takes as long as before and clients pay for reconnects that do nothing.
refuted.argument: In message #19 the author asked for an opt-in at the connection level for this reason: the signal is about one link, and proxies forward what they receive. In message #21 the author called the problem "not too bad" and reopened the ParameterStatus approach, which suggests the opt-in may be dropped. The material does not show whether the GUC version keeps it. Without an opt-in, every deployed proxy that forwards reported parameters has the wrong behaviour from the day the server is upgraded.
refuted.author_must_show: Does the disconnect_requested version report the parameter only to connections that asked for it, and how does an old pooler avoid forwarding it?

refuted.title: Privilege rule for pg_goaway_backend() is not stated
refuted.failure_scenario: On a shared cluster, a low-privilege role calls pg_goaway_backend() in a loop over pg_stat_activity pids, including backends of other roles. Every well-behaved pool keeps dropping and reopening its connections, so the cluster sees reconnect storms and extra authentication load. The other tenants only find the cause by reading server logs.
refuted.argument: v8 adds pg_goaway_backend() for any single backend (message #15), and the visible prose never says who may call it or whether it survives into the disconnect_requested GUC version. pg_cancel_backend() and pg_terminate_backend() limit callers to the same role, pg_signal_backend members, or superusers, with superuser backends protected. A request that is honoured by every compliant pooler is a cross-session action that needs the same limit. If it is granted to PUBLIC or skips the role check, any user can disturb other roles' sessions.
refuted.author_must_show: Does pg_goaway_backend() use the same role checks as pg_terminate_backend(), including pg_signal_backend and the protection of superuser backends?

critic.reasoning: The scenario assumes pg_goaway_backend() skips the role checks, but the proposal does not say that it does. The v8 code and docs are not shown, so this is an item that could not be checked.

refuted.title: A reported disconnect_requested GUC reaches poolers that replay ParameterStatus
refuted.failure_scenario: A replica enters smart shutdown and reports disconnect_requested=on. PgBouncer or Pgpool-II already tracks reported GUCs and passes them on to its clients, so those clients close their pooler connections while the pooler's server connections stay open. The replica still does not drain, and the clients reconnect for nothing.
refuted.argument: In message #19 the author asked for an opt-in at connection level so that old poolers cannot forward the signal. In message #21 the author called the cost of skipping it "not too bad" and turned to ParameterStatus, which proxies already forward and re-sync. The material does not say whether the GUC version keeps any opt-in. It also does not say how a GUC normally sent at the end of a query reaches an idle connection.
refuted.author_must_show: With the GUC design, what stops a pooler that does not know disconnect_requested from passing it to clients and causing reconnects that do not help drain the server?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1 for the opt-in and of replication-ondisk-2 for the idle timing.

refuted.title: Permanent libpq and protocol surface with no shown client consumer
refuted.failure_scenario: Core ships a new exported libpq function, a SQL function and a reported setting. No pooler or driver acts on them for several releases, so smart shutdown still waits for the pool's maximum lifetime. The project must still keep the interface stable whenever someone later wants different semantics, such as a deadline.
refuted.argument: In message #12 Tomas Vondra asked for a pooler or client proof of concept. In message #15 the author offered to write one, but none appears in the material. The demand shown comes from one pooler author (message #2) and one linked patch (message #4), and in message #20 Pgpool-II reported no need. The interface also changed three times, which makes it harder for a pooler to plan support against it.
refuted.author_must_show: Which pooler or driver has a working change that reacts to disconnect_requested, and how much faster does a replica switchover drain with it?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of demand-1. It also misreads message #20, where "No problem for Pgpool-II" answers the opt-in question and says nothing about need.

refuted.title: Proposal does not compare against idle_session_timeout for draining
refuted.failure_scenario: An operator starts a smart shutdown on a read replica, sets idle_session_timeout to a few seconds and reloads. The server then closes pooled sessions as soon as they sit idle. A committer reviewing the patch cannot tell what the new GUC, message, libpq function and SQL function add beyond this, so the case for a permanent protocol-visible addition is weaker.
refuted.argument: idle_session_timeout already makes the server close sessions that sit idle outside a transaction, and the drain case targets exactly those connections. No message in the thread mentions it. Its gaps are real: the client sees a FATAL error on the next checkout, and a busy pool whose connections are never idle that long does not drain. Those gaps would make the case for the proposal, but they are not shown with numbers or a pooler example (message #12).
refuted.author_must_show: For a pool draining under smart shutdown, what does idle_session_timeout fail to do that disconnect_requested does, and how often does that happen in practice?

critic.reasoning: The objection itself says idle_session_timeout ends sessions with a FATAL error that the client sees on next use, which is the error the proposal avoids. It also does nothing for pooler restarts, a main use case in message #3.

touch_points.reason: The server sends a new signal to clients, first as a GoAway message and now probably as a ParameterStatus for disconnect_requested.

touch_points.reason: v8 adds the SQL function pg_goaway_backend(), which needs a pg_proc entry.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The v1 patch adds PQgoAwayReceived() to libpq's exports.txt.

touch_points.reason: The CommitFest title names a new read-only disconnect_requested GUC.

touch_points.label: psql UX conventions

touch_points.reason: pg_goaway_backend() acts on another session, and the visible material does not state its privilege rule.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: see objection standards-compat-1: Reported GUC drops the opt-in that kept old poolers from forwarding

questions: Does the disconnect_requested version report the parameter only to connections that ask for it, and what do clients behind a current PgBouncer or Pgpool-II see?
When does the server send the disconnect_requested ParameterStatus to a client whose backend is idle, and which clients and proxies were tested with that timing?
Which pooler or driver has a working change that reacts to disconnect_requested, and how much faster does a replica switchover drain with it?
Does pg_goaway_backend() remain in the GUC version, and does it use the same role checks as pg_terminate_backend()?
Can the disconnect_requested value later carry the deadline or priority that Tomas Vondra and Zsolt Parragi asked for, without breaking clients that read it as a boolean?

committability.owner_note: Someone who knows the frontend/backend protocol, libpq and ParameterStatus reporting would have to own it. Several reviewers replied, but the visible material shows no committer taking it on.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a client-visible parameter and its timing rules for as long as drivers and poolers read it. Any exported libpq function also stays for good.
committability.author_follow_up: Good signs: the author sent v2 one day after the first review, reworked the design twice, and moved the entry to the next CommitFest on 2026-10-01.

priority.reason: Sites that drain replicas or restart poolers gain, and the patch is small, but it adds a lasting client-visible contract. The opt-in and idle-timing questions need an answer first; the GUC version of the patch was not read.

provisional_note: The GUC version and its thread are not visible, so its opt-in, its report timing and the fate of pg_goaway_backend() and PQgoAwayReceived() could not be checked. The backend idle-path cost also needs the code.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add new protocol message to change GUCs to be able to change protocol extension parameters
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a protocol message that lets a client set a GUC without a SET command, so poolers can see the change and some parameters can be set only at the protocol level. Over time the work became a patch set with a protocol minor version bump, min_protocol_version and max_protocol_version libpq options, and protocol parameters such as report_parameters.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the entry and moved the remaining protocol patches to the thread about longer cancel keys. Some pieces were committed here, including a libpq function PQfullProtocolVersion added in place of redefining PQprotocolVersion. The visible messages show no objection that rejected the core design.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: This required another rebase, but I've decided that I think it'll be most fruitful to continue the discussion on protocol changes in the thread about longer cancel keys[1].

precedents_retrieved.title: Use "protocol options" name instead of "protocol extensions" everywhere
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Heikki Linnakangas, Robert Haas, Jacob Champion, Laurenz Albe, Peter Eisentraut
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch replaces the term "protocol extensions" with "protocol options" in the docs and in a libpq error message, because "extension" suggests a link to Postgres extensions. No protocol options existed yet, so the author saw this as the time to settle on one name.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers did not agree on a new name. Heikki Linnakangas said "protocol option" suggests GUCs, Robert Haas found "protocol extensions" mildly clearer, Jacob Champion preferred keeping "protocol extension" with a docs note, and Laurenz Albe voted to keep "extension" because "option" already names other things in the docs. Peter Eisentraut rejected the patch for lack of consensus to change.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I don't think there is consensus for change, so I'm rejecting it.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add new protocol message to make GUC_REPORT configurable and use it for psql prompt substitution of %N with the current user
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a psql prompt escape %N that shows the current role. To keep the prompt current, it adds a new protocol message and libpq functions (PQlinkParameterStatus, PQunlinkParameterStatus) that turn GUC_REPORT on or off for a given setting during a session.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the patch and said he would resend it once Jelte Fennema-Nio's _pq_.report_parameters patch is committed. Peter Eisentraut suggested a GUC that lists the settings to report instead of a new protocol message. Jelte Fennema-Nio argued that proxies such as PgBouncer already re-sync GUCs, so a GUC-based design is less fragile for them than a new message type with its own connection state.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I think this is probably one of the core reasons why I would very much prefer GUCs over new message types to configure protocol extensions like this: It means proxies would not to keep track of and re-sync a new kind of connection state every time a protocol extension is added.

precedents_retrieved.title: Get rid of an extra error for client disconnection on Windows
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Tom Lane, Michael Paquier, Alvaro Herrera
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changed pgwin32_recv so that WSAECONNRESET from WSARecv is returned as EOF, as recv(2) does on Linux. This removes the "could not receive data from client" log message on Windows when a client exits without PQfinish().
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that WSAECONNRESET also covers a host reboot, a disabled network interface and a hard close, so treating it as EOF would hide real errors that should be logged. Michael Paquier and Alvaro Herrera judged that removing one log message did not justify that risk, and Michael Paquier marked the entry rejected.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I'm fairly concerned that this change would mask real errors that ought
to get logged.

precedents_retrieved.title: Password identifiers, protocol aging and SCRAM protocol
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch set moves password storage from pg_authid into a new pg_auth_verifiers catalog, allowing one verifier per protocol per role, with a superuser GUC (password_protocols) and a sanitize function used by pg_upgrade to retire outdated protocols. On top of this it adds refactoring patches and SCRAM-SHA1 authentication as a new password protocol.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Robert Haas argued that the work should move to the next release cycle: these are large, user-facing changes involving wire protocol changes, and they had received little detailed code-level review. He judged that they could not be completed safely in the three weeks before feature freeze, and he questioned whether there was consensus on the direction, including multiple password verifiers. The author agreed that the SCRAM patch (0009) needed more time than remained, and no committer took it on; Magnus Hagander said he lacked time in this CommitFest. The author marked the entry returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I don't see how we're going to get all of this into 9.6, and these are big, user-facing changes that I don't think we should rush into under time pressure.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "graceful shutdown" changes for Windows.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "graceful shutdown" changes for Windows.
Reverted commit(s): On Windows, close the client socket explicitly during backend shutdown.; On Windows, also call shutdown() while closing the client socket.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commits 6051857fc and ed52c3707 in HEAD (they were already
reverted in the back branches).  Further testing has shown that while
those changes do fix some things, they also break others; in particular,
it looks like walreceivers fail to detect walsender-initiated connection
close reliably if the walsender shuts down this way.  A proper fix for
this seems possible but won't be done in time for v15.

precedents_retrieved.title: Built-in connection pooler
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a connection pooler inside Postgres, with proxy worker processes that accept clients on a separate port and multiplex them over a small pool of backends per database and user. A session that changes session state, such as temporary tables, prepared statements or GUCs, is marked tainted and keeps a dedicated backend until the client disconnects.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why the entry was closed in 2021. An earlier commitfest entry was returned in 2020 because the patch needed a rebase and had waited on author for 6 weeks. After the 2021 resubmission, Antonin Houska reported that the patch did not apply to master and raised design issues, including the proxy's use of libpq inside the server, the static connection_proxies setting, walsender connections and unsynchronized shared memory; no reply from the author is shown.

precedents_retrieved.title: propagating replica identity to partitions
precedents_retrieved.summary: Make alter table ... replica identity on a partitioned table recurse to all partitions, and make new partitions take the parent's replica identity, mapping an index-based identity to the matching partition index. psql would also show the replica identity of partitioned tables.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew it for lack of time, with work still left in the patch. pg_dump had to emit the replica identity only after the index exists in all partitions, and a bug reported by Dmitry Dolgov was still open. Reviewers agreed with the recursion; the author planned to resubmit for November.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I've not had time to work on this issue, and there are a few remaining problems in the patch; mostly that I will need to change the way pg_dump represents the replica identity so that it is only defined when the index is dumped in all partitions rather than immediately after creating the index.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add and report the new "session_read_only" GUC pseudo-variable.
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a server-reported GUC (first "in_hot_standby", later "session_read_only") that is sent to clients in a ParameterStatus message, so clients learn without polling that a server is in hot standby or has left it. Later versions merged the hot standby state with default_transaction_read_only, used it in libpq's target_session_attrs, and added a new cross-backend signal to report the change.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane found an unresolved design issue: session_read_only combines default_transaction_read_only and RecoveryInProgress(), and the patch does not track intra-session changes to DefaultXactReadOnly. He asked for two separate GUC_REPORT variables, a new name and SIGHUP in place of the new signaling mechanism. The author agreed but sent no new version, and the entry was returned with feedback after that.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Looking through the thread, it seems like there's a pretty fundamental
design issue that hasn't been resolved, namely whether and how this ought
to interact with default_transaction_read_only.

get_extension_version
Threads: proposal - get_extension_version function

roaster_notes.note: No listed precedent records a rejection reason that applies here: P11 died on a read-only interaction this flag lacks, and P3 supports the GUC direction. The thread points to an earlier discussion only for the protocol-version pushback (message #5), which the proposal already answered by dropping the minor version bump.
The read-only reported GUC itself follows existing practice such as in_hot_standby, so I raise no objection to the mechanism.
The proposal has no on-disk, WAL, catalog or replication state. Walsenders were removed from the signal in message #8. The objections above are about the wire protocol only.

The read-only GUC and the shutdown-time signal expose only the fact that a smart shutdown has started, and the material shows no setting a user can change. The visible privilege question concerns pg_goaway_backend() alone.
Hot-path cost looks small from the prose: one procsignal at smart shutdown and an idle check. Without the GUC thread and its code, this cannot be confirmed.

The thread settled NOTICE as an alternative in message #19 because client_min_messages can suppress it. The move to a reported GUC uses the existing ParameterStatus mechanism and does not add a second one. I found no extension or contrib module that does this.
Demand exists but is thin: one pooler author in favour and no client adoption shown, so the honest outcome is not now, show demand.

warnings: CommitFest entry has 2 threads; only the earliest is read (https://www.postgresql.org/message-id/flat/DDPQ1RV5FE9U.I2WW34NGRD8Z%40jeltef.nl). Others: https://www.postgresql.org/message-id/flat/DJVLCL7PV7U6.35IJF87CZZ61Y%40jeltef.nl
